coverage_notes: Exhaustive sweep conducted across foundational theory, peer-reviewed HCI literature, contemporary research, and practitioner resources. Searches covered: (1) Horvitz 1999 foundational work; (2) seminal HCI authors (Shneiderman, Norman, Pirolli, Munzner, Tufte, Maes); (3) control allocation and autonomy levels; (4) mode switching and dynamic interaction; (5) trust, transparency, and explainability; (6) human-in-the-loop and interactive ML; (7) proactive systems and intervention timing; (8) user modeling and personalization; (9) shared autonomy in robotics; (10) decision authority and governance; (11) multi-agent coordination; (12) conversational and natural language interfaces; (13) visual analytics and exploratory analysis; (14) cognitive workload and task analysis; (15) context awareness and ambient intelligence; (16) uncertainty representation and communication; (17) recent CHI/UIST/TOCHI papers (2024-2025); (18) meta-analyses and systematic reviews; (19) LLM-based agents and agentic interfaces. Deduplication applied across multiple search result sets. Coverage includes T0 meta-analyses, T1 peer-reviewed conference papers, T2 seminal textbooks, and T3 high-quality practitioner/framework papers. Notable gaps defer to future phases: specific cultural/regional variations in mixed-initiative interaction design, domain-specific deployments beyond robotics/healthcare/knowledge work, and implementation case studies from production systems at scale.
